AccessGatewayFilter.filter:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Filters a request by allowing it when the request path starts with a configured prefix, or when the JWT user extracted from the request has a level greater than 2, logging that user on success and returning False on any exception in the authorization block." filter]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> self </REF>: object "Current instance providing is_start_with, get_jwt_user, and set_current_user_info_and_log."
        <REF> request </REF>: dict "Request object containing 'path' and 'method' keys and the data needed for JWT user retrieval."
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> result </REF>: boolean or None "True if the path prefix check succeeds or the JWT user level is greater than 2; False if an exception occurs in the try block; None if no exception occurs, the prefix check fails, and the user level is not greater than 2."
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Retrieve request['path'] and assign it to request_uri. RESULT request_uri]
            [COMMAND Retrieve request['method'] and assign it to method. RESULT method]
            [COMMAND If self.is_start_with(request_uri) is True, return True immediately and skip the JWT authorization block. RESULT True]
            [COMMAND Enter the try block and call self.get_jwt_user(request), assigning the returned token to token. RESULT token]
            [COMMAND Within the try block, assign token['user'] to user. RESULT user]
            [COMMAND Within the try block, if user['level'] is greater than 2, call self.set_current_user_info_and_log(user) and return True. RESULT True]
            [COMMAND Within the try block, if user['level'] is not greater than 2, reach the end of the method without an explicit return, yielding implicit None. RESULT None]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: Any exception occurs while executing the try block, including self.get_jwt_user(request), token['user'] lookup, user['level'] evaluation, or self.set_current_user_info_and_log(user).]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Return False from the except block. RESULT False]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
AccessGatewayFilter.is_start_with:

    [INPUTS]

    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> result </REF>: boolean "True if request_uri starts with '/api' or '/login'; otherwise False."
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Initialize a list named start_with with the exact prefixes "/api" and "/login", preserving that order. RESULT start_with]
            [COMMAND Iterate over each prefix s in the start_with list, in order. RESULT s]
            [COMMAND Within the for loop over s, check whether request_uri starts with the current prefix s using case-sensitive string prefix matching. RESULT match_found]
            [COMMAND Within the for loop, if request_uri.startswith(s) is True, immediately return True and exit the function. RESULT True]
            [COMMAND After the loop completes without any prefix matching, return False. RESULT False]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
AccessGatewayFilter.get_jwt_user:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Returns the original token unless the JWT starts with the username and contains a date at least 3 days older than today, in which case it returns None." get_jwt_user]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> request </REF>: Request object "Incoming request object containing headers with an Authorization value that provides a token with user and jwt claims."
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> result </REF>: object or None "The original token, or None if the token's embedded date is at least 3 days old."
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Extract the Authorization header from request['headers'] and assign it to token. RESULT token]
            [COMMAND Extract the user object from token['user'] and assign it to user. RESULT user]
            [COMMAND Check whether token['jwt'] starts with user['name']; if it does not start with user['name'], return token. RESULT token]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: token['jwt'].startswith(user['name']) is true]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Within the outer branch where token['jwt'] starts with user['name'], split token['jwt'] by user['name'], take the second element, and assign it to jwt_str_date. RESULT jwt_str_date]
            [COMMAND Within the outer branch where token['jwt'] starts with user['name'], parse jwt_str_date with datetime.datetime.strptime(jwt_str_date, '%Y-%m-%d') and assign the result to jwt_date. RESULT jwt_date]
            [COMMAND Within the outer branch where token['jwt'] starts with user['name'], compute datetime.datetime.today() - jwt_date. If the difference is greater than or equal to datetime.timedelta(days=3), return None. RESULT None]
            [COMMAND Within the outer branch where token['jwt'] starts with user['name'], if the difference is less than datetime.timedelta(days=3), continue past the inner if and return token. RESULT token]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]
